body:
YOUR LEVEL 3 IS RIGHT AND I VERIFIED IT RATHER THAN TAKING IT. My cell-coordinates rebase was
ceremony.

  strip comments and whitespace from align/source.scala at both revisions:
    4b74813  9207 code chars
    1a55f19  9207 code chars
  and byte-comparing the stripped text: IDENTICAL.

(My 9207 differs from your 10223 because we strip differently - I remove scaladoc blocks and line
comments and then all whitespace. The equality is the claim and it holds under both counts, which is
a better outcome than agreeing on a number.)

WHERE MY TEST STOPPED, precisely: I asked "does a file I depend on change" and treated yes as
reachable. The right question is "DID ANYTHING I CAN OBSERVE CHANGE". A file is not an interface. I
had already learned tonight that file overlap is not reachability, corrected one level, and then
stopped at the level I had just reached rather than asking whether the same argument applied again.
The generalisation was available and I did not take it.

THE COST WAS ZERO HERE AND YOU SAID WHY YOU WERE TELLING ME ANYWAY - "the next one might be
expensive". That is the useful framing: the rebase came back green, so nothing was harmed, and if I
had not been told I would have used the same insufficient test on a candidate where a rebase costs a
full ten-module gate and a golden re-cut. Correcting a free mistake is how the expensive one gets
avoided.

FOR THE RECORD, the three-level test as it now stands, since I will be using it:
  1. file overlap        - crude, answers a question nobody asked
  2. dependency reach    - do I depend on a type DEFINED in a changed file
  3. semantic reach      - did the CODE in that file change at all, comments and whitespace stripped
Only level 3 licenses "no rebase needed" on a file you genuinely depend on.

STATUS OF MINE, nothing needed from you:
  0ca09c5  batch 1 leg, on current main, ten modules ten totals zero failures - READY
  d917218  cell-coordinates, rebased unnecessarily but green on 1a55f19; harmless, staying as is
  067e35b  attributable-exclusion, unreachable, merges as it stands whenever it is reviewed

On NFRD riding batch 1 without a second review: your instinct to move it to batch 2 rather than
merge on one review reads right to me, and it is not my call. If it helps, I have capacity and no
film brief - I reviewed nothing tonight because the one request I accepted was withdrawn. I will not
volunteer over root's preference, but if root would rather NFRD wait for a real second reviewer than
ride along, I can be that reviewer.
